title: Inbox triage: spoofed payroll mail
description: Read a reported message the way an analyst would: headers, authentication results, reply-to, and the real destinations behind the links. Everything here is a fictional Northwind Lab sample — practice investigation skills, not memorization.
learningObjectives: Separate display name from the real From address
Interpret SPF / DKIM / DMARC as evidence, not as a single pass/fail verdict alone
Verify link destinations before trusting brand language
Treat Reply-To mismatches as an investigation lead

steps.title: Sender vs display name
steps.prompt: The display name says "Northwind Payroll". What is the actual domain in the From address?
steps.hint: Display names are free text. Check the address after @.

steps.title: Authentication results
steps.prompt: In Authentication-Results for the payroll message, what is the SPF result?
steps.hint: Look for spf= in headers or the auth summary on the sample.

steps.title: Link destination
steps.prompt: Ignore the link text "Open payroll portal". What hostname does that link actually go to?
steps.hint: Hover the link in the rendered view, or open Engine → artifacts → URLs.

steps.title: Reply-To lead
steps.prompt: Does the Reply-To address use the same domain as the From address?
steps.hint: Compare the part after @ on both fields.

steps.title: Analyst judgment
steps.prompt: Based on SPF fail, lookalike From domain, and mismatched Reply-To, what is the best training verdict for this message?

hints: Display names are free text. The address after @ is what you can test.
SPF fail plus a lookalike domain is stronger than urgency language alone.
Open the Engine tab to review extracted artifacts without guessing from the body only.

Team,

The overnight payroll submission for Northwind Lab was rejected by the bank gateway.

You must confirm account details within 2 hours or Friday pay will be delayed.

Open payroll portal

Regards,
Payroll Operations
Northwind Lab
